top_jobs.job: When I paid to win a first-time buyer and most never order again, help me reach them at the moment they usually reorder, with the right use, fit and reorder messages, so I make the ad cost pay back
top_jobs.metric: second order rate within 90 days of the first order

top_jobs.job: When the email platform says email made a big share of revenue, help me see what each flow and send really made from store orders, fix the flows that give margin away and keep only proven wins, so I pay for real results
top_jobs.metric: email revenue from store orders within 1 day of a click, and repeat orders gained against a holdout

top_jobs.job: When new sign-ups come in every day, help me turn them into first buyers within 72 hours with messages that fit what they already know and answer what stops them, so I do not waste the sign-up I paid for
top_jobs.metric: sign-up to first order rate within 7 days

top_jobs.job: When my top customers bring most of the profit, help me make them feel noticed with a personal letter and quiet early access, so I keep them buying and talking about us
top_jobs.metric: 12 month repeat rate and gross profit of the top 2 percent of customers against a held-back group

top_jobs.job: When a send could land in spam, break a law, promise something false or go unanswered, help me check before it goes and catch it after, so I keep the inbox and the customer's trust
top_jobs.metric: spam complaint rate and inbox placement on the main sending domain

jobs.job: Work out the median days between first and second order per first product, and set each post-purchase and win-back flow to fire on that day, not the default 90

inputs.need: orders with customer, product and date, 24 months
how long each product lasts in use, where it wears out or runs out

steps: Compute median and 75th percentile days to second order per first product, in code
Group products with a similar clock
Set the cross-sell email a few days before the median and the win-back after the 75th percentile
Hold out 10 percent of new buyers for 60 days
Read second order rate against the holdout
jobs.output: a timing table per product group and flows set to it, with a holdout running

watch.metric: second order rate within 90 days

jobs.job: Build a replenishment reminder per consumable or wear-out product, timed to when it runs out or wears out, with a one tap reorder link to the same size and colour
jobs.trigger: once per product, fired on each buyer's clock

inputs.need: variant, size and colour per past order

steps: Pick products bought 2 or more times by at least 10 percent of buyers
Set the reminder a week before the median reorder day
Build a reorder link that fills the cart with the same variant
Write 2 messages: a plain reminder, then a nudge with a reason to buy now that the offer rules allow
Read reorders from the flow against a 10 percent holdout
jobs.output: live reminders per product with a one tap reorder, and a holdout read

watch.metric: reorder rate per product from the reminder

jobs.job: Split the post-purchase flow for first-time buyers: thank you on day 0, a use or fit email before the parcel lands, a review ask 5 days after delivery, and a cross-sell on the reorder clock

inputs.need: top return reasons and use mistakes
review request timing in the reviews app

steps: Map today's post-purchase messages and remove any that clash with the reviews app
Write the use or fit email from the top 3 return and ticket causes
Move the review ask to 5 days after delivery, not after dispatch
Add the cross-sell on the buy-cycle day
Read returns for fit, review rate and second orders over 60 days
jobs.output: a first-time buyer flow with 4 timed messages and a 60 day read
jobs.next: review counts feed 07-14 (proof for new products); fit causes come from 06-15

watch.metric: returns for fit or wrong use, share of first orders

jobs.drives: second order rate and review count

jobs.job: When a return is logged, send a save note that offers the right size or an exchange first, then store credit, and track who buys again within 60 days

inputs.need: return events with reason and item

steps: Trigger on the return with the reason
For fit, suggest the right size using the fit notes
For other reasons, offer an exchange, then store credit
Send a plain note from a named person, not a promo
Read the share who buy again in 60 days against returners before the flow
jobs.output: a return save flow with one note per reason

watch.metric: returners who buy again within 60 days, share

jobs.job: Rebuild email and text revenue from store orders placed within 1 day of a click, per flow and per campaign, and put it next to the platform's own number
jobs.trigger: monthly, and before an agency renewal

inputs.need: clicks, opens and sends per message
orders with UTM source and time

steps: Tag every link with flow or campaign in the UTM
Match orders to a click within 1 day, in code
Sum per flow and campaign, and set it next to the platform's 5 day open-based number
Split new and repeat buyers
Write the gap in 1 line for the founder
jobs.output: a flow and campaign table with our number next to the platform's, split by new and repeat buyers
jobs.next: feeds 14-06 and the agency review in 26-reports

watch.metric: email revenue from store orders, share of total

jobs.drives: what we pay for email tools and agency against what it earns

jobs.job: Hold out 10 percent of new buyers from the post-purchase and win-back flows and 10 percent of text subscribers from texts for 60 days, and read the gap in repeat orders and profit
jobs.trigger: once, read at 60 days, then yearly

inputs.from: store platform plus unit costs from the finance shelf

steps: Add a random 10 percent holdout tag to each key flow's entry
Do the same for texts
Wait 60 days without changing the flows
Compare repeat orders and gross profit per person, in code
Keep, cut or change each flow and text program on the gap, and log it
jobs.output: a lift read per key flow and for texts, with a keep or cut call

watch.metric: repeat orders per 100 people, flow vs holdout

jobs.job: Reorder the cart and checkout flows: a plain reminder first, answers to the top checkout doubts second, and a discount only in the last message and only for first-time buyers

inputs.need: cart and checkout flow messages and results
top checkout doubts from tickets and polls

steps: Split into added to cart and checkout started flows
Message 1: the cart, the product image, no discount
Message 2: answer the top 2 doubts (shipping cost, returns, fit)
Message 3: a discount only for first-time buyers, within the discount rules
Read recovered orders and profit per recipient against the old flow
jobs.output: a 3 step cart and checkout flow that gives a discount only when needed

watch.metric: profit per recipient in cart and checkout flows

jobs.drives: discount cost as a share of revenue

jobs.job: Judge every email and text test on orders and profit per recipient, promote the winner to the flow standard (T0) that new flows copy, and write a fail note for losers with a date to recheck
jobs.trigger: after each test, and on each recheck date

inputs.need: test arms with sends, clicks and orders
unit costs for profit per recipient

steps: Set the main number before the test: profit per recipient, not opens or clicks
Run to the planned sample, not to a date
For a win, write the standard with the number, like 'plain text founder note ends every flow, +11 percent orders'
For a loss, write the fail note and 'do not rerun unless'
Recheck each standard after 6 months
jobs.output: an email standard list with proof and recheck dates, and a fail list
jobs.next: feeds 05-09 (brand standards) and every new flow build

watch.metric: tests judged on orders or profit, share

jobs.job: Split the welcome flow by what the sign-up already knows: cold sign-ups from a quiz or content get a problem and story series, warm ones who viewed a product get that product, proof and the offer inside 72 hours

inputs.need: sign-up source and pages viewed before sign-up
awareness level of each sign-up source and landing page

steps: Tag each sign-up source by awareness level
Branch the welcome flow: cold path and warm path
Cold path: problem, why old fixes fail, how ours works, proof, then the offer on day 3
Warm path: the product they viewed, reviews, the offer in the first email, a reminder at 48 hours
Read first orders in 7 days per path against the old single flow
jobs.output: a 2 path welcome flow tied to awareness level, with a 7 day order read per path

watch.metric: sign-up to first order rate within 7 days, per path

jobs.job: Put the answers to the top 5 pre-sale questions from the coverage matrix into the welcome and browse emails, one question per email, in the customer's own words
jobs.trigger: once, then when the matrix changes
steps: Take the top 5 questions by ticket count
Write a short answer email for each, headline in the customer's words
Place them in the welcome and browse flows where the doubt shows up
Check each against the claims and policies
Read click to order rate per email and pre-sale tickets from subscribers
jobs.output: 5 answer emails live in the welcome and browse flows

watch.metric: pre-sale tickets from subscribers per 1,000 sign-ups

jobs.job: Rank sign-up sources (pop-up, quiz, footer, checkout, ad lead forms) by first orders within 30 days and cost per buyer, and tune the pop-up's timing and offer on that

inputs.need: site conversion with and without the pop-up

steps: Count sign-ups and first orders in 30 days per source, in code
Add cost where a source has spend, like lead ads
Check site conversion for sessions that saw the pop-up vs not
Move pop-up timing to 8 seconds or exit, never on load, and test the offer
Grow the sources with the lowest cost per buyer
jobs.output: a source table with first orders and cost per buyer, and a tuned pop-up

watch.metric: first orders within 30 days per 100 sign-ups, by source

jobs.job: When a sold-out product comes back, alert everyone on its waitlist within an hour, only once stock is really live, in order of sign-up

inputs.need: waitlist sign-ups per product and variant
inputs.from: email platform or back in stock app

steps: Trigger on stock going above 0 for the variant, not on a planned date
Check stock covers at least 20 percent of the waitlist, or send in batches
Send email and text to the waitlist within 1 hour
Send a second note after 24 hours only if stock remains
Read orders per 100 on the waitlist
jobs.output: a restock alert that fires on real stock, with orders per 100 waiting

watch.metric: orders per 100 waitlist sign-ups within 48 hours

jobs.job: Rank customers by 12 month gross profit and recency, pick the top 2 percent, and have the founder sign a short personal letter to each, mailed in a plain envelope with no discount code
jobs.trigger: twice a year, and after each peak

inputs.need: open complaints or refunds to skip
a print and mail service for letters

steps: Rank customers by gross profit and last order date, in code
Take the top 2 percent and drop anyone with an open complaint
Hold back 20 percent of them at random for the read in 14-15
Founder writes a 5 line letter: thanks, one true detail about what they bought, a way to reach them
Mail it and tag each customer with the date
Say nothing about it in public channels
jobs.output: letters mailed to the top 2 percent, each customer tagged, and a held-back group

watch.metric: repeat orders from letter recipients vs held back

jobs.drives: 12 month repeat rate of top customers

jobs.job: Give the top customers quiet early access to new products and restocks 48 hours before the list, by private link, and keep them out of discount blasts

inputs.need: a hidden product link or password page

steps: Build the private link or hidden collection 3 days before launch
Send a plain note from the founder 48 hours early, no mention of 'VIP' or a tier
Remove the VIP segment from discount campaigns and cap them at 2 sends a week
Give a named reply-to person, not the no-reply address
Read early orders and sell-through from the group
jobs.output: a quiet early access send per launch, and a VIP segment kept out of discount blasts

watch.metric: orders from VIPs in the 48 hour window

jobs.drives: launch sell-through and repeat rate of top customers

jobs.job: Read the top customer program against the held-back group at 90 and 180 days, on repeat orders, gross profit and referrals, and keep it only if it pays
jobs.trigger: at 90 and 180 days after each letter round

inputs.need: cost of letters, gifts and time

steps: Compare repeat orders and gross profit per person, recipients vs held back
Count referrals and reviews from each group
Subtract the cost per person
Write keep, change or stop with the numbers
Log it in the ledger with a recheck date
jobs.output: a 1 page read of the program with a keep, change or stop call

watch.metric: gross profit per top customer, recipients vs held back

jobs.job: Route every reply to a marketing email or text into the helpdesk, answer within 1 business day, and track time to first reply and follow-ups owed
steps: Set the reply-to to a real inbox that feeds the helpdesk
Tag replies by flow or campaign
Set a 1 business day first reply target
Report weekly: replies, time to first reply, follow-ups owed, orders from repliers
Turn repeated reply questions into email copy fixes
jobs.output: every reply answered inside 1 business day, with a weekly report

watch.metric: time to first reply on marketing email replies

jobs.drives: customer satisfaction and orders from repliers

jobs.job: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the sending domain, spam rate in Google Postmaster and bounce rate per send each week, and run the repair steps when spam passes 0.3 percent
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and on any open rate drop across all sends

inputs.need: DNS records for the sending domain
bounces, complaints and clicks per send

steps: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass, and fix any that fail
Read spam rate and reputation in Postmaster
If spam passes 0.3 percent, send only to people who clicked or bought in 90 days
Widen the audience again step by step as spam falls under 0.1 percent
Log each step and the date
jobs.output: a weekly domain health line and a repair log when needed

watch.metric: spam complaint rate, Gmail

jobs.job: Before every send, check consent, text quiet hours for the buyer's state or country, and that every stock, deadline and offer line is true against the store and the brand record
jobs.trigger: before every campaign and every new flow
steps: Check every contact in the segment has consent for that channel
Check text send time against quiet hours in each recipient's time zone
Check 'last chance', 'almost gone' and deadline lines against real stock and end dates
Check claims against the claims shelf
Block or fix, and log the result
jobs.output: a pass or block per send with the line to fix

watch.metric: sends blocked before going out, and complaints after, count

jobs.job: Cap each person at 1 email and 1 text a day across flows and campaigns, and list who got 3 or more messages in a day last week
steps: Count messages per person per day for last week, in code
List people who got 3 or more and which flows overlapped
Set flow priority so a cart email pauses the browse email
Turn on the platform's frequency cap for campaigns
Read unsubscribes per 1,000 sends before and after
jobs.output: a frequency cap, a flow priority order and a weekly overlap list

watch.metric: unsubscribes per 1,000 sends

jobs.job: Stop mailing contacts with no click, site visit or order in 180 days after a 2 email goodbye, and watch the platform bill and spam rate fall

inputs.need: contacts with last click, visit and order dates
opens are not trusted alone because of mail privacy features
inputs.from: trust and access shelf (numbers not to trust)

steps: Build the segment: no click, no visit and no order in 180 days
Send 2 plain goodbye emails 5 days apart with a one-click stay button
Suppress everyone who did not click
Record the list size, bill tier and spam rate before and after
Re-run monthly
jobs.output: a smaller, active list and a lower platform bill

watch.metric: contacts billed and spam rate

new_enablers.name: Buy cycle clock
new_enablers.what: Works out from orders the median and slow-end days between first and second order, per first product and per consumable, and sets the day each post-purchase, replenishment and win-back message should fire.
inputs: orders with customer and product, 24 months
product use life from the founder, where known
powers: reorder reminders on the brand's own clock, not 90 days
a read on which first products bring repeat buyers

new_enablers.name: Flow map with store revenue
new_enablers.what: Every flow and message with trigger, timing, filters, copy and design, and results rebuilt from store orders placed within 1 day of a click, with a holdout per key flow. Shows the platform's own number next to ours.
inputs: email and SMS platform events and flow settings
a holdout group per key flow
powers: which sign-up sources turn into buyers

new_enablers.name: Send guard
new_enablers.what: Checks the sending domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), spam rate, bounces and list health weekly, and checks each send before it goes: consent, text quiet hours per state and country, frequency caps, and whether stock, deadline and offer lines are true.
inputs: Google Postmaster Tools and Microsoft SNDS
powers: mail that lands in the inbox
no text at 9 pm or to someone who never opted in
